cards.title: 'Lower Your Voice — Surely the Most Hateful of Voices Is the Voice of Donkeys'
cards.note: Surah 31:19 concludes Luqmān's counsel with 'Be modest in your walking, and lower your voice; surely the most hateful of voices is the voice of donkeys,' matching Story of Ahikar 2:11 on softening the voice and the loud-voiced ass.

discussion.view: Muslim scholars identify Luqmān as a pre-Islamic sage gifted with wisdom by God, whose proverbial counsels the Qurʾān endorses.
discussion.reply: The combination of addressing 'O my son,' enjoining a modest gait, commanding a lowered voice, and illustrating the admonition with the braying donkey comes directly from the ancient Aramaic and Syriac Story of Ahikar (2:11: 'O my son, bend thy head low down, and soften thy voice... if it were by a loud voice that a house was built, the ass would build many houses every day').

cards.quranEn: Be modest in your walking, and lower your voice. Surely the most hateful of voices is the voice of donkeys.’
quranHighlights: Be modest in your walking, and lower your voice. Surely the most hateful of voices is the voice of donkeys.’

sources.title: The Story of Ahikar (Syriac Recension)
sources.en: O my son! bend thy head low down, and soften thy voice, and be courteous, and walk in the straight path, and be not foolish. And raise not thy voice when thou laughest for if it were by a loud voice that a house was built, the ass would build many houses every day; and if it were by dint of strength that the plough were driven, the plough would never be removed from under the shoulders of the camels.
